solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One regularly getting more than tipsy cake

definitions.text: One regularly getting more than tipsy
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a habitual heavy drinker who soaks up liquor
second meaning: a light airy cake

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps getting drunk on a boozy trifle-like cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipsy cake' looks like one phrase, a sherry-soaked dessert; split it and the clue ends with two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A drunkard is called this because he soaks up drink, and the word is also a common light cake.

clue.text: Some air staff turned up for rich governor

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Some members of an air force staff stood up for a wealthy ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: PART and AS read upwards give SATRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in ancient Persia, and by extension any wealthy, despotic petty ruler.

clue.text: Pellet mill price for head of mining

indicators.note: one thing put for another means it takes that other's place in the word

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for price

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the letter being replaced in mill

explanation.surface: A pellet mill's price is set for the boss of a mining firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The M of MILL, which is the first letter of mining, is swapped for PR, leaving PRILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A prill is a small round pellet or globule, such as of fertiliser or metal.

clue.text: Vote against retaining primacy of rifles? Not in America

indicators.note: what retains something holds it within
primacy is first place, so only the opening letter counts

explanation.surface: A vote against keeping rifles first, a question about gun control in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: Nary, as in 'nary a one', is a US and dialect word for not one.
explanation.definitionFit: Nary is chiefly American dialect for 'not a' or 'never a', so it means not in American usage.

clue.text: Putting fertilizer around good for the rain tree

indicators.note: one thing put around another encloses it

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Spreading manure around a tree is good for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The G sits inside GUANO before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The guango is the rain tree, Samanea saman, a large tropical American shade tree.

clue.text: False story long ago tails off for moles

indicators.note: with their tails off, both words lose their last letters

parts.note: Chambers gives 'a false story' as a sense of tale

explanation.surface: A tall tale from long ago peters out, apparently about moles.
explanation.walkthrough: TALE and PAST each lose their final letter, giving TAL plus PAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Talpa is the Latin name and genus of the mole, used in English for the animal; talpas is the plural.

clue.text: Test taken by chief Greek commander

parts.note: Chambers lists 'a test' as a sense of trier
arch- means chief, as in archbishop

explanation.surface: A test is set by the head of a Greek army.
explanation.definitionFit: A trierarch was the captain of a trireme, a warship of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Former lover is dejected as before, injection of energy needed

indicators.note: an injection is put into something else, inside it

parts.note: amort is an obsolete word for dejected or lifeless, hence 'as before'
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An ex-partner is depressed once more and needs a boost of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former lover' reads like an ex; here 'former' only marks the word as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoret is an archaic word for a sweetheart or lover, so an old-fashioned word for a beloved.

clue.text: Plain diet neglected, like some duck?

indicators.note: something neglected falls into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plain diet gets ignored, as a duck might do.
explanation.definitionFit: The pintail is a duck with long pointed tail feathers, so some ducks are pintailed.

clue.text: Set about festive occasion with no end of homebrew

indicators.note: with no means something is taken away from the word
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A festive party sets about the drinking with no homebrew left.
explanation.walkthrough: WASSAIL loses its W, the final letter of homebrew.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack, and set about is an idiom for attacking someone.

clue.text: Basic piano installed in flat

indicators.note: something installed in a place is put inside it

parts.note: flat as in beer gone stale
P is the musical abbreviation for piano

explanation.surface: A basic piano is fitted in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment; it means stale.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a basic item, as in staple foods, the main or essential ones.

clue.text: African Union in rant about Albanian

indicators.note: about suggests letters moved around into a new order

parts.note: AU is the abbreviation for African Union

explanation.surface: The African Union features in a tirade about an Albanian.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arnaut is an Albanian, especially one serving as a soldier in the Turkish army.

clue.text: A little money on Hebridean islands for local powder

indicators.note: a little of a word is just a small part of it, its opening letter

parts.note: North and South Uist are islands of the Outer Hebrides

explanation.surface: A bit of cash spent on Scottish islands for some regional powder.
explanation.definitionFit: Muist is a Scots dialect word for musk, a scented powder, so it is local to Scotland.

clue.text: Bird given measure of feed for test in laboratory

explanation.surface: A bird gets a portion of food as part of a lab experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Titration is a chemical analysis measuring how much reagent reacts with a solution, a routine lab test.

clue.text: Fabled male who murdered needing protection accordingly

parts.note: under the aegis of means under the protection of

explanation.surface: A legendary killer needs protection as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: Aegisthus in Greek myth was Clytemnestra's lover, who murdered Agamemnon and was killed by Orestes.

clue.text: Minister's sermon a big hit

parts.note: ser. is the abbreviation for sermon
in cricket a skier is a ball hit high into the air

explanation.surface: A clergyman's sermon is a great success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests a clergyman to match the sermon; it is an Ottoman war minister. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraskier was the Turkish minister of war and commander-in-chief in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Stokes on strike showing force in Perth

parts.note: S is the symbol for the stokes, a unit of viscosity

explanation.surface: Ben Stokes, on strike at the crease, shows his power in Perth.
explanation.walkthrough: Stokes looks like the England cricketer batting in Australia; it is a physics unit. Perth is the Scottish city, marking a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stap is a Scots word meaning to cram or stuff, that is to force something in.

clue.text: Calm on cracking a century

indicators.note: something cracking another breaks into it and ends up inside

parts.note: an age, a very long time such as a century
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: Keeping calm while making a hundred runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is the cricket leg side, a convention worth knowing; 'a century' is a whole age, not the C or TON a solver reaches for first.
explanation.definitionFit: Alegge is a Spenserian form of allege, an old word meaning to allay or calm.

clue.text: Put about on train?

parts.note: the train of a gown or comet is its tail

explanation.surface: Asking whether something was put on board a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put about' reads as a sailing manoeuvre; it means spread a story around.
explanation.definitionFit: To retail gossip is to repeat it to others, to put it about or spread it.

clue.text: Quietly, I try to capture knight getting value for pawn

indicators.note: to capture something is to take it and hold it inside

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A chess player quietly tries to take a knight and get good value for a pawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The knight goes inside GO. 'Pawn' looks like a chess piece; it is the verb meaning to pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: To pignorate is to pledge or pawn something, from Latin pignus, a pledge.

clue.text: Fear working in lead for unsophisticated house

indicators.note: working suggests letters set in motion and rearranged
one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

explanation.surface: Fear of lead in a basic house.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a cheap house assembled from factory-made parts, a basic, plain kind of dwelling.

clue.text: Mountain hollyhock used to be slightly docked

indicators.note: docked means cut short, as a tail is docked

explanation.surface: A mountain plant used to be a little cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: A BIT loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasabi is a Japanese plant whose name translates as 'mountain hollyhock'; its root makes the green condiment.

clue.text: Foolish strike gets anonymous backing in plant

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: to ram is to strike hard
A is the abbreviation for anonymous

explanation.surface: A daft industrial strike wins the support of an unnamed plant worker.
explanation.walkthrough: SILLY, RAM and A, read backwards together, give AMARYLLIS. 'Plant' suggests a factory; it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The amaryllis is a bulbous flowering plant with large trumpet-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Jellyfish from sea north of the States?

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A jellyfish turns up from the ocean north of America.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'north of' puts MED above USA.
explanation.definitionFit: A medusa is the free-swimming bell-shaped form of a jellyfish, named for the snake-haired Gorgon.

clue.text: One crying out like a coward, some would say

indicators.note: what some would say means how the word sounds in certain speech

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, and in some dialects, chiefly rural American

explanation.surface: Someone shouting out like a coward, people might say.
explanation.definitionFit: A yeller is someone who yells, that is one who shouts or cries out loudly.

clue.text: Scottish noble in Sicily on vacation that's wet and sticky

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
a vacated word is emptied of its middle, leaving its outside letters

parts.note: losh is a Scots exclamation form of 'Lord'

explanation.surface: A Scottish lord holidaying in Sicily finds it humid.
explanation.walkthrough: Losh is a Scots minced oath for 'Lord', so it stands in for a lord in the clue's playful sense of noble.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloshy describes something slushy or sloppy, wet and sticky like mud or melting snow.

clue.text: Spots opening for Root to get trophy at Lord's

indicators.note: an opening is the very start, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the Ashes is the England-Australia cricket trophy, kept at Lord's, the London cricket ground

explanation.surface: Openings are spotted for Joe Root to win the Ashes at Lord's.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Root is an England batsman, so 'opening' reads as a batting opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: Rashes are outbreaks of red spots on the skin.

clue.text: Grass in a row overheard

indicators.note: overheard means caught by the ear, so it is the sound that matters

parts.note: serial means in a series, one after another

explanation.surface: A spy grasses on people in a row he has eavesdropped on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like the verb to inform; it is the plant family.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereals such as wheat, oats and barley are cultivated grasses grown for their grain.

clue.text: One fuel tariff initially staggered, not used currently

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the preceding word

explanation.surface: Someone was stunned by an energy tariff that no longer applies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not used currently' marks the answer as an obsolete spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Agast is an obsolete spelling of aghast, meaning shocked or staggered.

clue.text: Short book given by northerner, originally Finnish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: abbreviation for a book of the Old Testament
second meaning: an Estonian, of a Finnic people of northern Europe

explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' suggests taking a first letter; it says the Estonians share Finnic origins.
explanation.definitionFit: Esth abbreviates the Book of Esther and is also an old word for an Estonian, a Baltic Finnic people.

clue.text: Old tower mostly providing honey

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: An ancient tower largely supplies honey from its bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe and honey are both slang terms of endearment for a sweetheart or attractive person.

clue.text: Nurse surrounded by rolls of bark in South American trees

indicators.note: something surrounded by another sits within it

parts.note: a quill is a curled roll of dried bark, as of cinnamon
aia, or ayah, is an Indian nursemaid

explanation.surface: A nurse is wrapped in rolls of bark among trees in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Quillaia is a Chilean tree, the soapbark, whose bark yields saponin.

clue.text: Area with hides for grouse-shooters in Borders

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area
buts is a variant spelling of butts, screens behind which grouse-shooters wait

explanation.surface: A patch of moor with shooting hides in the Scottish Borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borders' looks like the Scottish region, apt for grouse moors; it is a verb. 'With' joins the hides to the area.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to border on or adjoin something, so 'borders' as a verb matches.

clue.text: Society girl quiet about old Jag

indicators.note: one thing about another wraps around it

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A debutante hushes everyone about her vintage Jaguar car.
explanation.walkthrough: SH wraps O. 'Jag' looks like the car; it means a drinking bout.
explanation.definitionFit: Debosh is an old form of debauch, a bout of excess, and a jag is a drinking spree.

clue.text: Repeated damage in northern steelyard

parts.note: bis means twice, an instruction to repeat

explanation.surface: Repeated damage at a steelworks in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A bismar is a kind of steelyard, a weighing balance, used in Orkney and Shetland.

clue.text: Extremely clever minor bagging first spot in Reading

indicators.note: bagging means catching and holding something inside
the first spot in a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A very bright child gets top marks in reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions plus wordplay. 'Extremely clever' looks like one phrase, and 'extremely' tempts you to take CR, the ends of clever; it is a definition. Reading is also an English town.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty can mean very, as in pretty good, and in an older sense means clever or ingenious.
